_doc: What the weather does to crops and trees (docs/WEATHER.md 'Weather and the harvest'; owner, 27 Nov; our own touch). Families as in data/catalog/crops.json and trees.json. `spoils_ripe`: a ripe crop of these families left out in this weather withers (Balance weather.spoil_grace_seconds after the weather comes), as growers know: rain rots ripe berries and flowers, storms flatten grain and rot cotton, frost kills the tender crops. Growing crops are never harmed. `loves`: a crop or tree that grew through this weather for at least Balance weather.love_share of its time gives Balance weather.loved_bonus more: sun sweetens berries, melons, grapes and cotton and the sun-loving fruit trees; rain feeds rice, beans and the tropical trees; frost sweetens roots and gives temperate fruit trees their winter chill; misty mornings give shade-grown herbs (tea) their flavour; among the blooms, roses, sunflowers and daisies want sun, irises and lilies rain, and tulips their winter cold. An Orchard or Bloom Garden gives the bonus for the share of what stands in it that had its weather. Plain rain still waters every crop (Balance seasons.rain_bonus). `blooms_spoil`: a Single Bloom on the farm, open and waiting to be picked, is spoiled by a storm (wind batters open flowers) and the tender ones by frost; tulips and irises take the cold, roses the frost; growing blooms are never harmed.
